Header: Colletotrichum capsici, Glomerella cingulata, C. acutatum , and C. coccodes खुसा ᭅनीको को ᮢे रोग

Prevention: Remove and destroy crop debris and weed plants especially if they are susceptible to the disease.
Rotate crop for 2-3 years with non-solanaceous crops (e.g. cowpea, cucumber, pea etc.)
Mulch to reduce rain splashes to avoid inoculum dispersal.
Avoid overhead irrigation, water the soil directly to keep leaves dry and reduce spore dispersal.
Harvest fruits as soon as they ripen.
Practice deep ploughing at the end of the season.
Monitoring: Monitor field for drying of twigs or branches from the tip (dieback) and irregular tan/ brown lesions with darker brown borders in leaves at weekly interval at vegetative stage.
Inspect fruit at ripening stage for sunken lesions with blackish fungal growth, usually in rings.
In humid weather, observe orange/pink spore masses on lesions.
Direct Control: Drain out excess water if the plot gets water-logged.
Without spreading the disease, carefully remove diseased plants, plant parts (diseased twigs) and fruit and dispose of in a pit (at least 50cm deep) outside the field or burn.
Restrictions: Use personal protection equipment (PPE) while using fungicides.
Seed treatment with captan 50% WP @ 2 gm per kg seed or carbendazim 50% WP @ 2 gm per kg seed
U (Unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use)
Spray copper oxychloride (COC) 50% WP @ 2 g/litre water at first visible symptom observed in leaves and twigs and during fruit setting period.
Spray carbendazim 50% WP @ 2 g/litre water during fruit setting period.
U, Carbendazim has 14 day waiting period.
